rationale: Evidence: iteration 6 is the best raced design (score 570.4). Moving the sensors forward from y=0.03 to y=0.05 m raised the oval finish rate to 20/20 and the s-bend finish rate to 9/20, and lifted slalom progress from 0.28 to 0.41. The lead distance is clearly the lever that works. Slalom is still 0/20, ending off track with max_error near the 0.06 m limit, and steering_oscillation there is about 0.30. Change (one variable): sensor y moves from 0.05 to 0.07 m, the upper end of the allowed range. This extends the look-ahead further so the correction starts earlier at the alternating slalom bends. Everything else stays fixed (x spacing -0.04 to 0.04 with 16 mm footprints, kp 3.0, kd 0.8, ki 0.02, base_speed 1.3, mass 0.6 kg, last_direction line loss), so the effect of look-ahead can be isolated. Expected result: slalom and s-bend max_error falls, and slalom progress rises above 0.5. Oval should stay near 100 percent completion. Hypotheses: (a) if the slalom still exits at max_error about 0.06 with no gain from y, steering authority is the limit, so kp should move to about 3.3 with kd held. (b) If steering_oscillation rises above 0.35, the far-forward sensors are amplifying jitter, so kd should drop toward 0.6. (c) If the oval stops completing, the forward lead is overshooting on straights, so y should return to about 0.06. Measurements wanted: completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation, control_effort and noise_robustness, per track.
